title: Load test scenarios for bounded autoscaling (spikes/ramps, SLO impact, no bound violations)
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
related_links: Confluence: Dedicated autoscaling SLOs and alerts (sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-autoscaling-slos-and-alerts.json)
GitHub: perf-canary PR-311 (bounded scaling ramp-up canary) (sources/github/perf-canary/pr-311.json)
GitHub: redwood PR-22057 (hotfix: cooldown/clamp stuck scale-down) (sources/github/redwood/pr-22057.json)
description:
Goal
Validate that Dedicated autoscaling with customer bounds (min/max) never violates bounds under realistic traffic patterns, and quantify impact to customer-visible SLOs during spikes/ramps. This ticket produces repeatable load test scenarios + perf-canary coverage so we can gate rollout by region/tier.

Why
We’ve had customer escalations around spend guardrails (max must be strict) and concerns that a too-low max causes throttling/latency spikes. We also need confidence that bounded behavior doesn’t introduce oscillation or bad cooldown interactions (see recent stuck scale-down bug class).

Scope
1) Add load test scenarios that:
- Exercise burst up to max, sustained load at max, and recovery back down while respecting cooldown/scale-rate limits.
- Exercise “max too low” behavior (intentional throttling/queue growth) to confirm we clamp + emit correct audit/metrics and that latency impact is observable.
- Exercise min floor behavior during low traffic and during drain/maintenance simulation (ensure we don’t scale below min via controller decisions; note infra may still temporarily dip due to drains depending on ADR semantics).
- Exercise predictive blending on/off and low-confidence gating paths (no overprovision beyond max; graceful fallback to reactive).

2) Define pass/fail criteria and dashboards to review per run:
- Hard requirement: bound violations = 0 (applied_replicas never > max, desired_replicas clamp_reason present when computed > max; applied_replicas never < min when controller is healthy and not in explicit drain simulation).
- SLO impact reporting: p95/p99 end-to-end latency and throttle rate during ramp, time-to-stable capacity (scale lag), queue depth peak, oscillation counter.

3) Integrate into perf-canary so we continuously run at least one bounded-scaling scenario in staging (and optionally a reduced-cost nightly in prod-canary).

Non-goals
- This ticket does not tune the autoscaling algorithm itself; it supplies data and regression coverage. Any tuning changes should be follow-up issues against ENG-2843/ENG-2845.

Environment / Harness
- Primary harness: perf-canary load generator (existing token-based QPS driver) pointed at a dedicated pool in staging.
- Pool config: dedicated test pool per region (start with us-west-2), hardware class aligned with design-partner rollout (e.g., L4/A10 class depending on fleet availability).
- Metrics source of truth: scaling decision metrics added in ENG-2846 (desired_replicas, applied_replicas, clamp_reason, scale_latency, oscillation counters), plus request latency/throttle metrics.

Test Scenarios
A) Ramp-up to max with burst enabled
- Setup: min=2, max=8, burst_to_max=true, cooldown_up=60s, cooldown_down=300s, scale_rate_limit_up=+2 replicas/min (or current defaults), predictive disabled.
- Load shape: linear ramp from baseline to max capacity over 4 minutes; then hold for 10 minutes; then ramp down to baseline over 6 minutes.
- Assertions:
  - desired_replicas should increase monotonically until at/near max; any overshoot must be clamped with clamp_reason=max_bound.
  - applied_replicas must never exceed max.
  - scale lag < SLO threshold (record time from queue depth crossing threshold to applied_replicas increase).

B) Instant spike (reactive) where max is hit
- Setup: min=2, max=6, burst_to_max=true, predictive disabled.
- Load shape: step function from baseline to ~150% of what max can sustain.
- Assertions:
  - clamp_reason=max_bound appears once desired > max.
  - throttle rate increases as expected (since max is intentionally insufficient), but system remains stable (no runaway retries; queue depth bounded by configured backpressure).
  - customer-visible dashboard fields are present (for later Console audit trail): “clamped to max” should be explainable via clamp_reason and decision log.

C) Max too low guidance scenario (UX/support readiness)
- Setup: min=2, max=3 (deliberately low), predictive disabled.
- Load shape: 30 min diurnal-ish wave that frequently demands 4–5 replicas.
- Deliverable output: a short run report we can reuse for Support/Solutions to show what metrics look like when max is too low (throttles, queue depth, clamp count).
- Assertions:
  - no bound violations
  - clamp metric cardinality stays bounded (no per-request tags; only per-pool/region).

D) Min floor during low traffic
- Setup: min=4, max=8, predictive disabled.
- Load shape: near-idle traffic for 20 minutes.
- Assertions:
  - autoscaler does not reduce applied_replicas below min.
  - if scale-down is blocked by min, clamp_reason=min_bound is emitted and applied_replicas remains at min.

E) Cooldown/clamp regression: scale-down should not stick at min
- Purpose: regression for the cooldown/clamp interaction that previously caused stuck scale-down behavior.
- Setup: min=2, max=8; run sustained load to reach 8; then drop load to near-zero.
- Assertions:
  - after cooldown_down, applied_replicas decreases toward min within expected time window.
  - no “stuck at intermediate” behavior; oscillation counter stays below threshold.

F) Predictive blending confidence gating (smoke)
- Setup: min=2, max=8; predictive enabled.
- Load shape: scheduled ramp with known periodicity.
- We will run twice:
  - F1: forecast confidence forced low (via test hook) -> expect fallback to reactive; no pre-scale.
  - F2: forecast confidence high -> expect earlier scale-up than reactive; still clamped to max.
- Assertions:
  - desired_replicas respects max in both cases.
  - compare p95 latency during initial ramp window: F2 should reduce spike vs F1 (record deltas; not a hard gate for initial release).

Pass/Fail Criteria
- MUST PASS:
  - applied_replicas never > max across all scenarios.
  - desired_replicas clamped deterministically when > max; clamp_reason set (max_bound).
  - no repeated oscillation above alert threshold (per SRE doc).
  - scale decision metrics emitted and queryable for each scenario.
- SHOULD PASS (report only; not gating for initial rollout unless egregious):
  - scale lag within target window in scenario A/B.
  - predictive high-confidence run reduces p95 latency during ramp vs reactive-only.

Deliverables
- perf-canary scenario implementation + CI wiring.
- Runbook snippet for “how to run bounded autoscaling load test” (command line, required env vars, where to find dashboards).
- One-page summary of results with links to dashboards + any anomalies found.

Implementation Notes
- Prefer running with a single pool per region to avoid fleet contention. Coordinate with Fleet Ops if capacity constrained.
- Use feature flag allowlist (ENG-2848) to ensure bounded autoscaling is actually enabled for the test pool.
- Keep token generation parameters stable (temperature, max_tokens) to reduce variance in GPU utilization.

Progress / Updates
- 2026-01-18 (Leila): Drafted scenario matrix (A–F) and aligned required metrics with Allison/Thomas (ENG-2846). Waiting on feature flag allowlist in staging.
- 2026-01-27 (Leila): Implemented scenarios A/B/E in perf-canary branch. Found missing clamp_reason tag for min-bound clamp in one path; filed follow-up note to Keiko (not blocking max-bound validation).
- 2026-02-03 (Leila): Ran A/B/E in us-west-2 staging. No applied_replicas > max observed. Captured scale-lag and latency graphs; spike test shows expected throttling once clamped at max.
- 2026-02-06 (Leila): Added predictive smoke (F) with confidence override hook; results are informational only. Opened a small doc note for Karthik/Yara about confidence threshold tuning.
- 2026-02-10 (Connor): Approved for merge once PR-311 lands; will use as rollout gate for design partners.

Result Summary (staging)
- Bounds correctness: PASS. No max-bound violations observed across A/B/E/F runs.
- Cooldown/clamp regression: PASS after hotfix baseline (PR-22057). Prior to hotfix branch, E reproduced ‘slow/stuck’ behavior intermittently; now resolved.
- Observability: PASS. clamp_reason=max_bound visible and low-cardinality. desired vs applied replicas charts present.
- SLO impact: Recorded. Ramp-up p95 latency spike reduced in predictive-high-confidence run vs reactive-only (directionally good), but not treated as gating.

Follow-ups (not required for closing)
- Consider adding a dedicated “max too low” warning text in Console using the same scenario C graphs as reference (ties to SUP-4874).
- Add explicit drain simulation scenario once min semantics during maintenance are finalized per ADR-0142.

Closure
Implemented in perf-canary PR-311; scenarios are now runnable in staging as part of bounded autoscaling rollout gates.
